fields.value: Discourses of ageism: a scoping review

dsDescriptionValue.value: Age is a fundamental category through which we organize and interpret the external world alongside gender and race. Previous studies have focused on chronological approach in understanding the aging phenomenon; while age, as a category, is embodied in our society, related to culture and shared representations in specific settings. Examination of discourses and social interactions can give a deeper understanding of how age is jointly constructed and whether inclusion or discrimination processes unfolds at this micro level of analysis. A scoping study method is used to explore and describe current research on age and ageism in interactions and discourses in order to identify research gaps. Main databases for social sciences were searched with keywords and papers were identified with inclusion and exclusion criteria. A descriptive and thematic synthesis is developed on the selected papers in order to define the methods used, the population and setting selected, the main findings reported and the contribution that qualitative studies can give on aging topic. Research gaps were identified which include need for studies about age in interaction and discourse. Further research that extends beyond self-reported cross sectional surveys is necessary to achieve a more complex understanding of the construction of age in specific settings and its relation with discriminative practices.
